content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm having trouble connecting to my [product_name]. I originally installed the software on a desktop using [product_name] [version_no] and tested it successfully. Now, the device is deployed at the site, and I'm attempting to connect with a MacBook via a thunderbolt to RJ45 adapter. The adapter itself works, and when I open the software, I see a green line indicating connection between the Mac and the device, but there's a red question mark over the device icon. Although the correct IP address, gateway, and subnet are detected, pressing refresh fails to bring the device up for connection. If anyone has suggestions, much appreciated. Thanks in advance.
Are both the [product_name] and the Mac within the same IP subnet?

Thank you for the reply. At first, the subnet wasn't the same, and when the prompt appears asking if I'd like to connect to the same subnet, I select yes, but then the connection fails. Any advice is appreciated. Thanks in advance.
Which version of [product_name] software are you using on your Mac?
I'm using [version_no] for both the device and the original program.
I'm not very familiar with Macs. Apologies, but hopefully another user here can assist you.

Hello [user_name], I don't have much experience with Macs either, but I have seen similar issues occur with Windows XP. In those cases, I had to ensure the IP addresses of the device and the computer matched before launching the software. Have you tried running the software within a Windows virtual machine or using Boot Camp? [user_name] (translated with Google)
Thank you for the suggestion. I haven't tested this yet, but will give it a try. Thanks again.

analysis.insight_summary: Users experienced challenges connecting [product_name] hardware to a MacBook via a thunderbolt-to-RJ45 adapter, even with correct networking configurations. While the software recognizes the hardware on the network, full connection could not be established or displayed. Contributors noted possible OS compatibility and virtualization-related problems, showing some uncertainty and a lack of comprehensive cross-platform troubleshooting guidance.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate straightforward and dependable connectivity between [product_name] software and hardware when using a MacBook, including support for virtual environments. They also look for clearer troubleshooting instructions and better error messaging when problems arise.
